subject: General Knowledge
description: Inventor-invention pairs + discovery history + Nobel-laureate level facts

questions.explanation: Alexander Graham Bell patented the telephone on 7 March 1876 (US Patent 174,465). Edison invented the phonograph and electric light bulb; Tesla developed AC power; Marconi pioneered long-distance radio.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Penicillin — the first widely used antibiotic — was discovered by:
questions.explanation: Alexander Fleming, 1928, at St Mary's Hospital London — noticed mould (Penicillium notatum) inhibited bacterial growth. Shared 1945 Nobel with Florey and Chain, who turned it into a usable drug. Pasteur pioneered germ theory and vaccines; Koch identified tuberculosis and anthrax bacilli; Salk developed polio vaccine.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Match the SCIENTIST with their discovery. A. Isaac Newton.  B. Marie Curie.  C. Albert Einstein.  D. Charles Darwin. List-II: 1. Laws of motion + universal gravitation. 2. Radioactivity (isolated polonium, radium). 3. Theory of relativity, photoelectric effect. 4. Theory of evolution by natural selection.
questions.explanation: Newton — Principia (1687). Curie — only person to win Nobels in two sciences (Physics 1903, Chemistry 1911). Einstein — Nobel 1921 for the photoelectric effect; relativity followed. Darwin — Origin of Species (1859).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Who discovered the LAW OF GRAVITATION?
questions.explanation: Newton's universal gravitation (F = G m₁m₂/r²) was published in Principia Mathematica, 1687. The famous falling-apple story (at Woolsthorpe Manor) is roughly contemporaneous but likely embellished.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The World Wide Web (WWW) was invented by:
questions.explanation: Tim Berners-Lee invented the WWW at CERN (1989-1991) — proposing HTTP, HTML, and the first browser. He is NOT the inventor of the Internet itself (which evolved from ARPANET; Vint Cerf and Bob Kahn designed TCP/IP). The Web is a layer on top of the Internet.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Consider the following Indian scientists and their contributions. 1. Homi J. Bhabha — father of India's nuclear programme. 2. Vikram Sarabhai — father of India's space programme. 3. C. V. Raman — discovered the Raman Effect (1928), won Physics Nobel 1930. 4. S. Chandrasekhar — published the Chandrasekhar limit for white-dwarf mass; won Physics Nobel 1983. Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: All four correct. Bhabha founded TIFR (1945) and AEET/BARC. Sarabhai founded PRL and later led ISRO — vision that India should use space for development. Raman — first Asian Nobel in sciences. Chandrasekhar — Indian-born, later US citizen; Nobel for stellar-structure work; nephew of C. V. Raman.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The first effective polio VACCINE was developed by:
questions.explanation: Jonas Salk developed the inactivated (injectable) polio vaccine, licensed 1955. Albert Sabin later developed the oral live-attenuated polio vaccine (1961-1962). Jenner (smallpox, 1796) and Pasteur (rabies, 1885) are the older vaccine pioneers.
